name: Sodom and Gomorrah
charge: Grievous sin; inhospitality and violence against strangers
summary: Cities whose sin was grave enough that its cry reached heaven. When two visitors lodged with Lot, the men of the city surrounded the house demanding them. Judgment fell the next morning.
offense: The prophets later name the fuller charge: pride, fullness of bread, careless ease, and no help for the poor and needy (Ezekiel 16:49-50), a hardness that showed itself in the mob at Lot's door. The cry against the cities was great before the messengers reached Lot's house (Genesis 18:20-21). The men then surrounded it, demanded the guests, threatened Lot when he resisted, and pressed upon the door. Even after the angels struck them with blindness, they wearied themselves seeking the entrance (Genesis 19:4-11). Abundance had not produced mercy, and correction did not turn the mob from its purpose. Abraham had pleaded that the righteous not be destroyed with the wicked; the Judge of all the earth distinguished the household brought out from the city overthrown (Genesis 18:23-25; Genesis 19:29).
judgment: Fire and brimstone from the Lord out of heaven (Genesis 19:24), overthrowing the cities and the plain (Genesis 19:25). Lot's wife, looking back, became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). Jude records the cities as an example of judgment upon fornication and strange flesh (Jude 1:7), and Peter sets their overthrow beside the deliverance of just Lot (2 Peter 2:6-9).

verses.text: And the Lord said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;
I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which is come unto me; and if not, I will know.
But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
And they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.
Then the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven;
And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.
But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good.

Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.
When the ungodly perished, she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.

Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.

For regarding not wisdom, they gat not only this hurt, that they knew not the things which were good; but also left behind them to the world a memorial of their foolishness: so that in the things wherein they offended they could not so much as be hid.
Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.
Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.

text.text: And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;
And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:
(For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)
The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished:

entries.commentary: The three men who stood by Abraham were angels of the Lord, and they had bodies: their feet were washed with water, they rested under the tree, and they did eat. Be careful how you deal with people, for some have entertained angels unawares. Abraham hastened to serve them. He commanded his household; he told Sarah, Make ready quickly. That is the level of his hospitality and his leadership.

Sarah was barren from the beginning and it had ceased to be with her after the manner of women; she laughed within herself at the promise of a son. The Lord answered the thought she never spoke: Wherefore did Sarah laugh? She denied it out of fear, and He said, Nay, but thou didst laugh. The Most High sees what is within the mind. Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

The Lord said, I know Abraham, that he will command his children and his household after him. The man is the leader who makes the rules and keeps his house in the way of the Lord. What makes a great husband and father is commanding the household in the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment. Where men walk away from justice and judgment, they cannot properly command their household.

The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah was great and their sin very grievous. The iniquity of Sodom was pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness; she strengthened not the hand of the poor and needy, was haughty, and committed abomination. The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law.

Abraham drew near and negotiated with the Most High because his nephew Lot dwelt in Sodom; that is why he pleaded for the city. Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? Abraham reasoned from fifty righteous down to forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty, and ten, and the Lord said, I will not destroy it for ten's sake. Below ten there was no more negotiating, and the Lord went His way.
Lot sat in the gate and pressed the two angels into his house, because he knew the men of Sodom. He made them a feast, and they did eat; angels have bodies and functions like men.

The men of Sodom, old and young, all the people from every quarter, compassed the house and demanded the men, that we may know them. To know in scripture is to lie with: Rebekah was a virgin, neither had any man known her. The whole city, both small and great, was given to this wickedness.

Lot went out and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. This is Genesis, way before [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18); sodomy was already wickedness and already unlawful before the law was written at Sinai. They pressed on Lot to break the door, and the angels smote them with blindness, small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

Lot's sons in law took him as one that mocked, and they perished. When the warning comes, treating it as a joke is death. While Lot lingered, the angels laid hold on his hand, the Lord being merciful to him. Then the instruction: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee; escape to the mountain.

The angel told Lot, Haste thee, for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. The destruction waited on the righteous being brought out, the same way the angels in [Revelation 7](/bible/revelation/7) hold the four winds until the servants of God are sealed. When Lot entered Zoar, the Lord rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. Those cities are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire; what was done there on a small scale is done in spiritual Sodom on a greater scale, and the example stands. Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct.

Lot's wife looked back, against the instruction, and became a pillar of salt: a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.

Lot's daughters thought Sodom had been the whole world and no man was left on the earth to give them seed, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him; he perceived not when they lay down nor when they arose. Do not take any wayward idea from this: uncovering the nakedness of thy father is against the laws of the Most High. It was unlawful then and it is unlawful now. The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the Ammonites, unto this day. In this teaching those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.

The word of the Most High came to Ezekiel to cause Jerusalem to know her abominations: her birth and nativity is of the land of Canaan, her father an Amorite and her mother a Hittite. This is describing how we were acting as heathens, to make it plain. In the day she was born her navel was not cut, she was not washed, not salted, not swaddled; no eye pitied her, and she was cast out in the open field to the loathing of her person. When the Most High passed by and saw her polluted in her own blood, He said unto her, Live; He caused her to multiply as the bud of the field, and she increased and came to excellent ornaments.

When the Most High passed by and looked upon her, her time was the time of love; He spread His skirt over her, covered her nakedness, sware unto her, and entered into a covenant with her, and she became His. He washed her with water, anointed her with oil, clothed her with broidered work and fine linen, decked her with ornaments, bracelets, a chain, a jewel, earrings, and a beautiful crown of gold and silver. She was exceeding beautiful and prospered into a kingdom, and her renown went forth among the heathen for her beauty, for it was perfect through the comeliness the Most High had put upon her. This is how the Most High took us, built us up into a mighty nation, and beautified us.

But she trusted in her own beauty and played the harlot because of her renown, and poured out her fornications on everyone that passed by. We got haughty, we trusted in our own beauty, and we began to play the harlot; the scriptures then explain what that means. She took her garments and made high places decked with divers colors, took the fair jewels of the Most High's gold and silver and made herself images of men, and set His oil, meat, fine flour, and honey before them for a sweet savour.

She took her sons and daughters, whom she had borne unto the Most High, and sacrificed them to the images to be devoured, causing His children to pass through the fire. In all her abominations and whoredoms she did not remember the days of her youth, when she was naked and bare and polluted in her own blood.

After all her wickedness the Most High cries woe, woe unto her; she built herself an eminent place and made a high place in every street, at the head of every way. Those high places in every street are the churches of today; here in America we see the coexist mindset, accepting every religion, while the Most High gave us the commandments, and now those religions have become a stronghold unto us. She committed fornication with the Egyptians, her great-fleshed neighbors, the same people that enslaved us four hundred years, much like we do today, provoking the Most High to anger.

Therefore the Most High stretched out His hand, diminished her ordinary food, and delivered her to the will of them that hate her, the daughters of the Philistines, which are ashamed of her lewd way. She played the whore with the Assyrians and yet could not be satisfied, and multiplied her fornication in the land of Canaan unto Chaldea, and still was not satisfied.

The Most High asks how weak her heart is, seeing she does all these things as the work of an imperious whorish woman; He gave us everything and we were not satisfied, chasing the philosophies, doctrines, and religions of the nations. She is not even as a harlot who scorns hire, but as a wife that commits adultery, taking strangers instead of her husband, giving gifts to all her lovers and hiring them to come unto her. -

Wherefore, O harlot, hear the word of the Most High: because her filthiness was poured out through her whoredoms with her lovers and idols, and by the blood of her children, He will gather all her lovers, both loved and hated, against her and discover her nakedness unto them. He will judge her as a woman that breaks wedlock and sheds blood, give her blood in fury and jealousy, deliver her into their hand to throw down her eminent place, strip her of her clothes, take her fair jewels, and leave her naked and bare. This is spiritual and physical: we do not control the distribution of our music, so the most vile music is put out for us and our children, showing us naked and in compromising positions, and that is what has been glorified here in America.

They shall bring a company against her, stone her, thrust her through with swords, and burn her houses, executing judgments in the sight of many women. The Most High will cause her to cease from playing the harlot and give no more hire, and then His fury and jealousy shall rest and He will be no more angry. Because she did not remember the days of her youth but fretted Him in all these things, He recompenses her way upon her own head.

Everyone that uses proverbs shall use this proverb against her: As is the mother, so is her daughter; she is her mother's daughter that loathes her husband and children, and loathe means hate. Her mother was a Hittite and her father an Amorite; her elder sister is Samaria and her younger sister is Sodom, yet she was corrupt more than they in all her ways. The iniquity of Sodom was pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness, and she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy; yet Samaria did not commit half of Jerusalem's sins, for Jerusalem multiplied her abominations more than them and justified her sisters, who are more righteous than she.

When the Most High brings again the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and of Samaria and her daughters, then He will bring again the captivity of Jerusalem in the midst of them, that she may bear her own shame. In the day of her pride Sodom was not so much as mentioned by her mouth, but now she bears her lewdness and abomination, having despised the oath in breaking the covenant.

Nevertheless the Most High will remember His covenant with her in the days of her youth and establish unto her an everlasting covenant. This is why the new covenant, the covenant of [Hebrews 10](/bible/hebrews/10) and [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31), is made only with His people; the notion that our oppressors, who glorified our fall, get the same reward is absolute foolishness and makes no biblical sense. When He is pacified, she shall remember her ways, be ashamed, and never open her mouth anymore because of her shame, and she shall know that He is the Lord. -
